newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr hurts mark, helps Paris stocks to record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr hurts mark, helps Paris stocks to record.

text.p: The rampant dollar paused just below a six-year high against the weary mark on Friday, thirsty for more gains but blocked by signs of sellers waiting in the wings.
The continued strength of the U.S. currency, which made a brief sally above 1.84 marks, gave the French and German share markets further support, driving the Paris bourse to another record close.
Currency dealers said the apparent tolerance of Germany's Bundesbank for a weak mark and the lack of support from the central bank's council meeting on Thursday had lifted the dollar.

"Unless Europe blows up, people are going to keep selling marks," said one trader. "And even if we see a meltdown in EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) and it doesn't go ahead, mark buying will be short-lived because the Germans need low interest rates to boost growth."

The Bundesbank's move yesterday to set a repurchase rate for just two weeks of its four-week summer recess gave the market brief pause for thought, however, suggesting that the bank was prepared to adjust monetary policy if need be.

A press statement after Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting, its last before the four-week summer recess, said the central bank was paying attention to developments in the mark and financial markets.
The dollar ended at 1.8345 marks after touching a fresh six-year high earlier of 1.8403. It was at 1.8315 late Thursday in Europe.
The dollar was also up against the Swiss franc, climbing above 1.51 to reach its highest since August 1993. It was at 1.5145 in late trade having been as high at 1.5176.
In Europe's share markets, London's FTSE 100 failed to make any progress after a subdued performance on Wall Street and ahead of an onslaught of company earnings next week.
The leading index ended 11.4 points lower at 4,851.5 for a net loss of 25 points on the week. Wall Street was down around 15 points when London closed.

"Volumes are beginning to drop off and business is slowing down for the summer recess. Concerns about interest rates are slowing the market down but it lacks any major impetus to move either way at the moment," said the head of market-making at one leading London brokerage.
The FTSE 100 had started the day modestly higher as a squeeze in selected stocks continued and a 28-point gain in New York sent the Dow to another record close on Thursday, its third in a row.
But the early rally soon petered out as investors remained wary ahead of the interim reporting season with the pound still trading at seven-and-a-half year highs.
Corey Miller, UK strategist at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said the stock market was looking tired after its spirited run to the brink of the 5,000 level last week.

"We're reacting to a perception of liquidity coming in but we have a deteriorating situation with interest rates and currency problems. All it would take would be one piece of bad news to take the market down." he said.
German shares closed a lacklustre floor session down nearly half a percent after trading sideways to cap a record-breaking week.
The DAX-30 index ended bourse dealing down 18.10 points at 4,317.64 -- about 90 points off Wednesday's all-time high of 4,406.09 -- as most shares failed to gain much impetus from the strong dollar.
But dealers said Friday's pause should not keep the DAX from continuing its upward charge until nearing resistance pegged at around 4,400 points.
"For next week I expect the market to continue rising," one trader said, and the Ibis DAX index of post-bourse electronic trading closed up 48.02 points at 4,368.54.

French stocks were in bullish mood, and the CAC-40 index ended 52.41 points, or 1.76 percent, at 3,025.94, a new record close. The previous record was set on Wednesday when the index closed at 3,003.53.
The market was encouraged by the stronger dollar and Wall Street's overnight close at a record high.
Rhone-Poulenc SA shares were up 4.2 percent at 259 francs after the chemicals group reported a 20.2 percent rise in second-quarter net income. Brokers said the results were excellent.
Peugeot Citroen rose an impressive 7.25 percent to 695 francs, helped by recent recommendations on the French car sector. Brokers said Peugeot is catching up with Renault's recent rally.
CURRENCY CLOSING LEVELS
The dollar was at 1.8345 marks and 116.75 yen compared with 1.8295 marks and 115.85 yen in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKET CLOSING LEVELS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 11.4 points at 4,851.5.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended down 18.10 points at 4,317.64.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 52.41 points at 3,025.94.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $324.05 an ounce after ending in London at $322.65 on Thursday.
